title: Enterprise RBAC matrix and audit-log retention roadmap
creator: Maya Patel
description: Goal: Define and deliver an enterprise-grade RBAC (role-based access control) matrix and a configurable audit-log retention framework that satisfies SOC2/ISO evidence requirements, supports SSO/SAML user mappings, and enables per-customer retention/service tiers.
acceptance_criteria: RBAC matrix published with canonical roles, permissions, and least-privilege mappings for all Console and API surfaces
Audit-log retention implemented as a per-organization policy with three retention tiers (90d default, 1y enterprise, custom up to 7y/legal-hold) and exports to customer-managed storage
UI and API to view, request, and change retention settings with appropriate approvals/audit trail
Evidence export playbook documented for SOC2 auditors and internal compliance team
Automated daily snapshot of retention settings and policy changes recorded in product audit logs
End-to-end tests and a canary rollout plan that proves no data leakage and maintains SLOs for read/write operations to logs
decisions: Adopt per-organization retention configuration instead of per-route by default to reduce UI complexity; expose per-route override in advanced settings
Default retention set to 90 days for all new tenants to balance storage cost and typical investigation windows
Enterprise tier will allow managed 1-year retention; custom retention up to 7 years available via signed contract/legal-hold only
Export design will support pushing encrypted logs to customer GCS/Azure Blob/AWS S3 with KMS/HSM integration for key control
RBAC roles will be derived from an access-control matrix mapping to SOC2 control families (CC6, CC7) and ISO27001 Annex A controls
open_risks: Storage cost for multi-year retention could exceed forecast if 5+ large customers opt in; need cost model and quota guardrails
Export availability SLAs may vary by customer storage config; must highlight in docs and contract terms
Complexity in mapping SSO identity provider group claims to our canonical RBAC roles — some IdPs have inconsistent group casing/attributes
Potential performance impact from long-retention queries on the audit-log search endpoint; require secondary index or archival tier
